items.text: Hendrix lost the side one master tape in a London taxi, and most of that side was remixed in one overnight session.
items.why: Recording: 'Hendrix lost the master tape of side one of the LP, leaving it in the back seat of a London taxi ... remixed most of side one in a single overnight session'.

items.text: 1 December 1967
items.why: Infobox: 'Released: December 1, 1967'.

items.text: May to June and October 1967, Olympic Studios, London
items.why: Infobox: 'Recorded: May–June, October 1967', 'Studios: Olympic , London'. (Recording section also mentions abandoned Houston Studios sessions and Mayfair Studios time, but the infobox gives Olympic.)

items.text: Chas Chandler
items.why: Infobox: 'Producer: Chas Chandler'.

items.text: Polydor, Track (UK), Reprise (US), Barclay (France)
items.why: Infobox: 'Labels: Polydor / Track (UK) Reprise (US) Barclay (France)'.

items.text: Are You Experienced had been finished by late April 1967, and this album came out seven months after that debut's release.
items.why: Recording: 'Following the completion of Are You Experienced at the end of April 1967'; Lead: 'only seven months after the release of the group's highly successful debut album'.

items.text: After that, the band kept up its regular recording sessions at Olympic Studios in London.
items.why: Recording: 'continued their schedule of regular recording sessions, returning to Olympic Studios in London'.

items.text: On May 4 they began composing material for a follow-up LP, starting with a Noel Redding song about hippies called She's So Fine.
items.why: Recording: 'on May 4 to begin composing material for a follow-up LP ... started the session by working on a Noel Redding original that he had written about hippies, titled "She's So Fine"'. Close paraphrase (six-word run 'composing material for a follow-up LP') but under seven words.

items.text: Chas Chandler produced and Eddie Kramer engineered, with George Chkiantz as second engineer.
items.why: Recording: 'With Chas Chandler returning as producer and Eddie Kramer returning as engineer, along with George Chkiantz as second engineer'.

items.text: The basic tracks went onto four tracks: drums on two, bass on a third, and rhythm guitar on the fourth.
items.why: Recording (unattributed quote): 'I would fill the four basic tracks with stereo drums on two of the channels, the bass on the third, and Jimi's rhythm guitar on the fourth'. The quote describes a habitual method ('would'); the note states it flatly, acceptable.

items.text: Chandler, Hendrix and guests Graham Nash and Gary Leeds stomped on a drum riser to create percussion for If 6 Was 9.
items.why: Recording: 'a percussion effect created by Chandler, Hendrix, and guests Graham Nash and Gary Leeds stamping their feet on a drum riser'. Copied run 'Chandler, Hendrix, and guests Graham Nash and Gary Leeds' (nine words, mostly names). Note the pack is internally inconsistent: Personnel credits foot stomping to Redding, Chandler, Leeds and Nash, not Hendrix.

items.text: Hendrix played recorder on that track too, though he had no formal training on the instrument.
items.why: Recording: 'Hendrix played a recorder on the track ... despite his complete lack of formal training with the instrument'.

items.text: Noel Redding had a tape of the lost mix, and the tape was so wrinkled it had to be pressed flat with an iron.
items.why: Recording: 'the lost mix of "If 6 Was 9". Bassist Noel Redding had a tape recording of this mix, which had to be smoothed out with an iron as it had gotten wrinkled'. The section never says which mix was lost (only the hook mentions the taxi); the pack says it was the If 6 Was 9 mix.

items.text: The Hendrix Estate released a box set, The Jimi Hendrix Experience: Bold As Love Sessions, on 7 November 2025.
items.why: Release and reception: 'The Hendrix Estate released, "The Jimi Hendrix Experience: Bold As Love Sessions" ... Box Set November 7, 2025'.

items.text: It has 66 tracks, among them demos and alternate takes, and both the stereo and the mono mixes of the album.
items.why: 'It contains 66 Tracks including Demos and Alternate takes plus the Stereo and Mono versions of the album'.

items.text: The Blu-ray in the set includes a Dolby Atmos mix.
items.why: 'The Blu-Ray contains Both of the 1967 Stereo and Mono versions of the album plus a Dolby ATMOS mix'.

items.text: Cat Talking to Me, recorded in June 1967, came out later on the posthumous album West Coast Seattle Boy: The Jimi Hendrix Anthology, in 2010.
items.why: Recording: June 5 session on 'Cat Talking to Me'; 'It was later included on the posthumous album West Coast Seattle Boy: The Jimi Hendrix Anthology (2010)'. Copied run 'on the posthumous album West Coast Seattle Boy: The Jimi Hendrix Anthology', mostly the title.

items.text: Sounds from Hendrix's guitar travel across the stereo image and seem to revolve around you, with feedback running through the track.
items.why: Music and lyrics: 'incorporates microphonic and harmonic feedback ... stereo panning effect in which sounds emanating from Hendrix's guitar move through the stereo image, revolving around the listener'. Title matches.

items.text: Its lyrics came from The Spanish Castle, a dance hall now in Des Moines, Washington, where Hendrix played with local rock bands as a teenager.
items.why: Pack: 'a dance hall in what is now Des Moines, Washington, near Seattle where Hendrix jammed with local rock groups during his high school years'. 'what is now Des Moines' means the place is now called Des Moines; 'a dance hall now in Des Moines' implies the hall still stands there today.

items.text: Hendrix's guitar runs through a Leslie speaker here, a first for him, and the speaker gives the sound a wavering effect.
items.why: 'On "Little Wing" Hendrix plays his guitar through a Leslie speaker for the first time (a revolving speaker which creates a wavering effect...)'.

items.text: Hendrix plays recorder on it, and some of the percussion is Gary Leeds and Graham Nash stomping their feet.
items.why: Recording: 'Hendrix played a recorder on the track'; Music and lyrics: 'some of the percussive effects were created by Gary Leeds (from the Walker Brothers) and Graham Nash stomping their feet'. Title: pack gives 'If Six Was Nine' (US edition spelling 'If 6 Was 9'), so the US spelling is acceptable.

items.text: Its guitar works through chordal arpeggios, and the track fades out on tremolo-picked double stops.
items.why: 'His guitar playing throughout the song is marked by chordal arpeggios and contrapuntal motion ... The track fades out on tremolo-picked thirty-second note double stops'.

missed: The title track's coda features the first recording of stereo phasing, and the cover (Hendrix and the band as forms of Vishnu, designed without his approval, banned in Malaysia) is left out entirely; also the backwards guitar solos on 'You Got Me Floatin'' and 'Castles Made of Sand', with Roy Wood and Trevor Burton of the Move on backing vocals.
